title: CAE Copilot: a validated toolkit for structural CAE and plate vibroacoustics

creators.name: Singh, Baij Nath
creators.affiliation: Bennett University, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India

description:
An open, browser-based toolkit for structural computer-aided engineering and the vibroacoustics of thin plates. It requires no installation, no network connection and no user account, and runs entirely client-side.

Script generation. Produces ready-to-run input decks for ABAQUS (Python), ANSYS (APDL), LS-DYNA (keyword) and MATLAB across static, modal, buckling, harmonic, explicit-impact and acoustic-radiation analyses. Each generated script carries the corresponding analytical result in its header, so a finite element run can be checked against an independent solution immediately.

Materials module. Functionally graded plates under power-law, sigmoid and exponential gradation with Voigt, Mori-Tanaka or Reuss homogenisation, referenced to the physical neutral surface so that bending-stretching coupling vanishes identically. Classical lamination theory with full ABD assembly and symmetry, balance and bend-twist diagnostics. Shear-corrected sandwich panel analysis with face yielding, core shear and face wrinkling margins. A parametric study module sweeps any of eleven design variables and exports results as CSV or LaTeX.

Boundary conditions. Natural frequencies are obtained from the exact Levy transcendental solution wherever a simply supported edge pair exists, and from a Rayleigh-Ritz formulation using characteristic beam functions otherwise, covering arbitrary combinations of simply supported, clamped and free edges.

Validation. Verified against Leissa (1969) across ten edge-condition cases with a maximum error of 0.028 per cent, and against classical closed-form results for laminated and homogeneous plates. The complete validation suite is distributed with the software and may be re-run independently.
